name: Progesterone
interpretation:
Progesterone Level (ng/mL or nmol/L)
Interpretation
Pre-Ovulation (Follicular Phase)
Low progesterone levels during the follicular phase (before ovulation) are normal. This helps prepare the body for ovulation and the subsequent release of an egg.
Peak Ovulation (Mid-cycle)
A significant increase in progesterone levels is observed during the mid-cycle, around the time of ovulation. This surge in progesterone prepares the body for potential pregnancy.
Post-Ovulation (Luteal Phase)
After ovulation, progesterone levels continue to rise, reaching their peak during the luteal phase. This phase is essential for preparing the uterine lining for embryo implantation.
Pregnancy
In the case of pregnancy, progesterone levels remain elevated throughout the first trimester. Progesterone is crucial for maintaining the pregnancy and supporting fetal development.
Non-Pregnant
If pregnancy does not occur, progesterone levels decline, leading to the shedding of the uterine lining during menstruation.
Low Progesterone Levels
Low progesterone levels during the luteal phase or pregnancy may indicate a potential issue with ovulation or insufficient support for pregnancy.
High Progesterone Levels
High progesterone levels outside of the normal luteal phase or during early pregnancy may suggest certain medical conditions or hormonal imbalances.
